newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-STEWART KEEPS ZIMBABWE AT BAY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-STEWART KEEPS ZIMBABWE AT BAY.

text.p: Alec Stewart spearheaded England's push towards a commanding second innings total on the fourth day of the second test against Zimbabwe at Harare Sports Club on Sunday.
At tea, Stewart was 70 not out in an England total of 137 for three, an overall lead of 78.
Stewart struck six boundaries from 183 balls and, during the course of his innings, overtook Pakistan's Saeed Anwar as the highest test run scorer in this calendar year.
England made a poor start to the afternoon when Dave Houghton took a good tumbling catch at short extra-cover to remove Nasser Hussain for six.
It was the second wicket of the day for leg-spinner Paul Strang who had removed opener Nick Knight, caught by Alistair Campbell at slip for 30, during the morning session.
At 89 for three England, who conceded a first innings lead of 59, were in trouble with a lead of just 30.
But the Surrey pair of Stewart and Graham Thorpe, 25 not out, dug their heels in and took England towards the safety zone with an unbroken fourth-wicket partnership of 48.
